statement: Qualitative hypotheses registered before FM2 flies. They contain no numeric prediction by FlameLedger.

hypotheses.text: At 29% O2 and 8.2 psia (FM2 Test 3), the Synergy Pro Navy fabric sustains upward flame spread in lunar gravity.
hypotheses.basis: NASA's FM2 plan states that Tests 1 to 3 should burn to threshold (E13). NASA authors expect partial gravity to increase flammability limits for some materials (E11).
hypotheses.refuted_if: The fabric fails to ignite, or self-extinguishes without sustained upward spread, at the Test 3 atmosphere.

hypotheses.text: The fabric's lunar-gravity flammability limit will not lie between its microgravity and normal-gravity limits. It will be lower than both.
hypotheses.basis: In NASA's drop-tower data, the lunar-gravity limit is below both the microgravity and the 1g limit for all three materials tested (E15).
hypotheses.refuted_if: When 1g and microgravity limits for the same fabric are available, the lunar-gravity limit falls between them.

hypotheses.text: At 25% O2 and 8.2 psia (FM2 Test 4), the outcome is closer to the flammability threshold than at 29%: a shorter burn, or no ignition.
hypotheses.basis: This follows NASA's own stated expectation that Test 4 is not expected to ignite (E13), and NASA's design target for the material (E18).
hypotheses.refuted_if: The Test 4 burn is as long as, or longer than, the Test 3 burn.
